topic_summary: Analysis of free movement of workers within the European Union, examining the contested federation-membership kernel read as integration-primary (mobility as economic imperative requiring supranational enforcement) versus member-sovereignty-primary (welfare state protection and labor market control at national level). The contest manifests as judicial expansion via CJEU versus legislative containment by member states, with asymmetric cost-bearers: displaced local labor and welfare systems in receiving states versus constrained mobility and demographic loss in sending states.

key_entities: Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) - judicial authority interpreting Article 45 TFEU expansively
Member States - retain welfare system responsibility and labor market sovereignty
European Commission - coordinates social security rights across borders
14 million intra-EU mobile workers - primary beneficiaries of free movement regime
Receiving states (Germany, Spain, Italy, France) - host majority of mobile workers
Sending states (Romania, Poland, Portugal, Bulgaria) - experience demographic loss
Unskilled workers in receiving states - compete with mobile labor
Treaty of Maastricht (1992) - established Union citizenship as legal foundation
key_tensions: Judicial activism (CJEU expansive interpretation) vs member state sovereignty (welfare eligibility restrictions)
Economic integration imperative (single market completion) vs welfare state integrity (national social protection systems)
Mobile worker rights (Article 45 TFEU) vs local labor protection (wage competition and job displacement)
Sending state demographic stability vs receiving state service capacity
key_mechanisms: Transitional restrictions (up to 7 years for new member states) - sovereignty carve-out mechanism
Welfare coordination (not harmonization) - member states retain system design authority
CJEU teleological interpretation - expands 'worker' definition and related rights beyond treaty text
key_absences: Enforcement mechanisms for implementation gaps - Commission infringement proceedings exist but member state non-compliance persists
Democratic accountability pathway for CJEU rulings - no mechanism for member state override of judicial expansion into reserved domains

omegas.description: No mechanism exists for member state override of CJEU rulings that expand EU competence into reserved domains. Is this a design feature (preventing sovereignty reassertion) or a Snare (judicial activism without democratic check)? The absence of an accountability pathway may itself be the extractive mechanism.
omegas.source: Absence Inventory (§1.1) - democratic accountability pathway for CJEU rulings

omegas.description: Analysis focuses on intra-EU mobility. Third-country nationals posted workers regime (carved out by CJEU and Commission) represents a parallel constraint system with different authority structure. Does this create a two-tier mobility regime where member state sovereignty is differentially constrained?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) - third-country nationals mentioned in extraction but not decomposed

omegas.description: Brexit represents the only case of a member state exiting the federation-membership kernel entirely. Does the 52% Leave vote validate the sovereignty_reading's claim that integration-primary interpretation extracts unsustainably from receiving state populations? Or does it demonstrate that the hybrid_reading failed to provide sufficient coordination mechanisms?
omegas.source: Extraction (§1.1) - Brexit referendum as political backlash; tests kernel reading validity

omegas.description: Integration_reading and sovereignty_reading hold contradictory axioms about the locus of legitimate authority over labor mobility (supranational vs national). Hybrid_reading attempts to reconcile through proportionality doctrine. Does proportionality review constitute a genuine third framework, or does it collapse into one of the two primary readings depending on CJEU composition?
omegas.source: §1.3-K Axiom Contradiction Declaration - testing whether hybrid_reading is structurally independent or unstable

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Three readings identified from contested kernel decomposition. Integration_reading and sovereignty_reading hold contradictory axioms about authority locus (supranational vs national). Hybrid_reading attempts reconciliation through proportionality but may be unstable (omega_axiom_contradiction_scope). Deferred axes are mechanisms downstream of selected readings or upstream mountains with lower distinctiveness.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Federation membership as shared commitment to free movement of workers, stabilized in Article 45 TFEU and Union citizenship provisions (Treaty of Maastricht 1992)
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between CJEU (supranational judicial interpretation) and member states (legislative authority over welfare and labor markets). CJEU grounds interpretive legitimacy in teleological reading prioritizing economic integration; member states ground legitimacy in democratic accountability and retained sovereignty over social protection.
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Interpretive Capture (Pattern 3) - CJEU absorbs drift through expansive interpretation of worker definition and citizenship rights, while member states resist through implementation gaps and transitional restrictions. Revision of Article 45 TFEU is institutionally possible but politically blocked; drift accumulates in case law rather than treaty text.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Integration_reading holds that legitimate authority over labor mobility resides at supranational level (CJEU/Commission) as necessary for single market completion. Sovereignty_reading holds that legitimate authority over labor mobility resides at national level (member state legislatures) as core democratic sovereignty. No single coherent framework can hold both axioms simultaneously - accepting supranational authority as legitimate requires rejecting national authority as ultimate, and vice versa.
